findings.assessment: Valid helper-level rejection expectations. Only guaranteed outputs are compared; neither changed fallible owner nor value participates. Conditional execution does not authorize changing a recipe-approved conditional output.
Valid for the explicit two-transaction helper fixture. Only baseTransaction is traversed; balancingTransaction is ignored. Mutation and deletion of its distinct intent escape checking.
Valid complete-effects expectation. The loop checks presence of base intents without rejecting extra finalized intents. This added intent contains new financial outputs, not merely proof metadata.

Valid fail-closed helper expectation. Truthiness of fi.ttl gates the comparison, so removing the approved expiration skips validation. This is an expiration-preservation gap, not evidence of a real transaction with an absent SDK-required property.

testAssessment.independence: Each fixture creates fresh Maps and independently clones both intent Maps. Mutations do not change the recipe; the control establishes this shape is accepted.
testAssessment.errorConvention: assert.throws matches existing helper rejection behavior. Its broad form does not prove any future exception has the intended cause.
testAssessment.rootCauses: Six cases exercise four omissions: fallible outputs, balancing transaction, extra intents, and missing TTL.
limitations: Plain synthetic objects have empty inputs/signatures, fake owner/type strings, and no signatureData method; they are not signed, proven, deserialized, or balanced transactions.

validateSignedRecipe would reject these fixtures with no signed inputs before fundUnshielded reaches this helper. The diagnostic does not establish reachability through that path or a submit/ledger exploit.

The union of disjoint base and balancing Maps is an explicit unit-test model. These files do not establish the exact pinned SDK finalization/merge semantics or that arbitrary added economic intents can arise from it.
No signature/order association, shielded effect, fee, gross allowance, serialization, proof, or ledger acceptance claim follows from these seven tests.
